Shopify Custom App vs Shopify App Store App: Many get confused when choosing between them. But not every store problem requires custom coding; there will be a point where you have to genuinely think about that.

Because it could save you from either overpaying for development you didn’t need, or stretching an App Store app past what it can actually do. Here’s how to make that call.

The Bottom Line

A Word of Caution

The Decision Test

The Real Cost Difference

When an App Store App Is Enough

What Each Option Actually Is

What Each Option Actually Is

An App Store app is a ready-made solution, built to work across many stores, with standard features and predictable setup. A custom app is built specifically for your store, with functionality tailored to your exact workflows.

One important 2026 update: as of January 1, Shopify closed the old admin-based flow for creating new custom apps. Custom apps are now built and managed through Shopify’s Dev Dashboard instead. Existing custom apps still work fine, but if you’re building new, the process now goes through a proper development environment, not a quick admin setting.

When an App Store App Is Enough

  • Standard, well-defined needs. Personalization, reviews, SEO tools, basic email flows — these are common enough that mature, well-built App Store apps already solve them.
  • You want to validate first. If you’re not sure a feature will actually move the needle, an app lets you test it without committing to a custom build.
  • Budget and speed matter more than a perfect fit. App Store apps are faster to install and far cheaper than custom development.
  • Unique business rules. If your workflow doesn’t match how any App Store app is built — custom order tagging, vendor-specific logic, non-standard pricing rules — you’re not going to find an off-the-shelf fit.
  • Deep integrations. Connecting Shopify to an ERP, a custom CRM, or a warehouse system usually requires more precision than a generic integration app offers.
  • High volume or performance-critical needs. At scale, a generic app’s limitations, rate limits, and generic data handling become real bottlenecks.
  • You’re building something no one else needs. If the App Store simply doesn’t have a category for what you’re solving, that’s your answer.

Ready-made apps are flexible within their boundaries. The key phrase is “within their boundaries”; they won’t stretch to fit deep, business-specific logic.

When Custom Development Is Justified

The Real Cost Difference

App Store apps are typically a monthly subscription, often $10 to $100+. Custom apps are a different scale entirely: a focused, single-workflow custom app can start around $2,500 to $15,000, while more complex, multi-integration builds run well beyond that. Custom development is an investment, not an impulse decision.

The Decision Test

Ask: Is this a standard category of problem, or does it involve business logic and integrations unique to how you operate? If it’s standard, an app almost always wins on cost and speed. If it’s genuinely unique, custom development is what actually solves it, rather than forcing your business to bend around a generic tool.

A Word of Caution

Two mistakes show up often: Expecting an App Store app to fully customize around unique needs it was never built for, and building a custom app with no plan for who maintains it once the person who built it moves on.

The Bottom Line

Start by checking if a mature App Store app already solves your problem. If it genuinely can’t, because of unique rules, deep integrations, or scale, that’s when custom development earns its cost.

Not sure which side of that line your need falls on?

Our team builds Shopify custom apps, integrations, and full-stack solutions for exactly these situations, and can help you figure out honestly which one you actually need.
